title: bug: the check's offline npm ci installs candidate bytes from a same-version file: spec in an unprotected package.json, despite the approved lockfile
description: guest-supervisor.py install_dependencies runs `npm ci` against the protected package-lock.json, but npm 11.19 (the pinned toolchain's) checks package.json against it by version only. With the lockfile byte-identical, a candidate package.json spec `file:../stub/is-number-7.0.0.tgz` (same name and version) installed the stub's bytes offline from an empty cache (CQ-R13 probe, npm 11.19.0), so check-evidence's dependencies boundary (host-offline-cache, lockfile-sha512) does not hold; `overrides` is likely a second route. CQ-R13's checkpoint already refuses an npm-shrinkwrap.json or .npmrc, requires a regular package.json and pins --workspaces=false; the remaining fix needs a design choice, e.g. install from the approved lockfile's root entry in a root-owned staging dir, protect package.json, or verify node_modules/.package-lock.json against the approved lockfile after the install. Build on CQ-R13's guest-supervisor.py checkpoint; the change alters supervisorSha256, so CERTIFICATION.md reports must be re-run on it.
definitionOfDone: A candidate that changes an unprotected package.json, adds overrides, or otherwise points a dependency at non-cache bytes gets no install of those bytes: the check fails closed, with a test per route.
The approved-lockfile install from the offline cache still passes (KI1, DC5 and certify canary-check stay green).
